instruments.name: Kick
instruments.description: Foundation 4-on-the-floor pulse — sits on every quarter beat of the Kick 4bar pattern. Provides the sub and low-band weight of the mix (~30 % RMS share at -21 LUFS). Centered (pan 0). Was the broken element fixed earlier: fm_amt flipped from -0.6 to +0.6 so the pitch now sweeps down (click → boom) instead of up (plopp).

patch.name: Kick
patch.description: 808/909-style synth kick. Sine oscillator with two ADSR envelopes: env-1 drives the amp (D=250 ms, no sustain) for body; env-2 modulates the oscillator's exponential FM input (D=80 ms, fm_amt=+0.6) for a downward pitch sweep — pitch attack ~85 Hz, settles to the played note in release. Tight body, no harmonics above ~1 kHz. Critical parameter: osc-1 fm_amt MUST be positive — negative values invert the sweep and produce a "plopp".

instruments.name: Snare
instruments.description: Backbeat snare on beats 2 and 4 (Snare 4bar pattern). Boosted +6 dB during mix-pass (track volume 2.0) — was originally 12 dB below the other elements which was too restrained even for an Amiga module aesthetic. Now sits ~5 dB below the bus average (LUFS -26). Slight left pan (-0.15) to balance the right-panned lead.

patch.name: Snare
patch.description: Hybrid noise/osc snare. White noise + low-level saw oscillator summed into a state-variable bandpass filter (cutoff 1.8 kHz, res 0.35, drive 1.2 for bite). Single ADSR (D=220 ms, no sustain) shapes both the amp and the filter envelope (env_amt 0.25). Broadband 2–4 kHz core; pitch confidence near zero, which is correct — this is intentionally inharmonic.

instruments.name: Bass
instruments.description: Harmonic anchor — plays the root motion of the Am–G7–Fmaj7–G four-bar progression. Square-wave timbre with a downward filter sweep gives it acid-ish movement under the lead. Largest RMS share in the mix (~33 %). Panned slightly left (-0.2) to clear stereo space for the lead.

patch.name: Bass
patch.description: Square/pulse bass with closed filter sweep — classic acid topology. Oscillator's odd-harmonic content (odd/even ratio ~+65 dB) gives the hollow square character. Filter envelope opens the cutoff at attack and decays it down, producing the downward centroid sweep (337 → 276 Hz). Key-tracking on the filter keeps the timbre consistent across the bass register.

instruments.name: Lead
instruments.description: Melodic top voice. The Lead 4bar pattern is octave-doubled (32 notes / 6.0 avg polyphony with the bass), tracing the Am/G7/Fmaj7/G progression. Panned right (+0.3) to open the stereo image opposite the bass/snare.

patch.name: Lead
patch.description: Square-wave melodic lead mirroring the bass topology one octave up. Pure odd-harmonic timbre (odd/even ratio ~+90 dB). Filter envelope produces a downward centroid sweep (1.16 kHz → 1.0 kHz) over each note. Locked tightly on pitch (sub-1-cent error at C4). Six audible harmonics, THD around -9 dB.

instruments.name: Hi-Hat
instruments.description: Eighth-note timing reference added during the mix-pass to fill the missing high-band content (pre-fix mix had almost no energy >5 kHz). Velocity-accented on beats, ghosted off-beats. Track volume 2.0 to bring LUFS up to -31 (5 dB below snare). Carries ~40 % of the mix's high-band energy. Slight right pan (+0.2).

patch.name: Hi-Hat
patch.description: Minimal closed hi-hat. White noise → state-variable highpass (8 kHz, mild resonance 0.1) → VCA with a 50 ms decay envelope (no sustain, 20 ms release). No oscillator, no key tracking — pitch input is ignored, every note plays the same brushed-air color. Centroid lands around 14 kHz; ~99 % of the energy sits in the >5 kHz band.

global.awe_description: Subtle small-room glue. Concrete box 8×5×3 m, 18 % wet, 25 % air absorption. Adds early-reflection shimmer in the 5–15 kHz band and breaks the perfect-mono image without changing the harmonic balance. Disable for a dry studio reference.
